Deliberately NOT underlined: IS, CONTAINS, CHARACTERS, FOR, ARE. (Confirmed at 300 dpi: 'CHARACTERS' has no rule beneath it while 'RECORDS' directly below it does; 'REPORT'/'REPORTS' are underlined while the following 'IS'/'ARE' are not.)
claim.markdown_says: FD file-name-1 / [ IS EXTERNAL [ AS literal-1 ] ] / [ IS GLOBAL ] / [ BLOCK CONTAINS [ integer-1 TO ] integer-2 { CHARACTERS / RECORDS } ] / [ record-clause ] .  — emitted as loose prose lines, with no code fence and no 'Figure notes' paragraph anywhere for Format 2 or Format 3
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining is the standard's only marking for required vs optional words, so dropping it erases the required/optional distinction for eleven words in these two formats — e.g. it no longer records that CHARACTERS is an optional word while RECORDS is required, or that IS may be omitted from 'IS EXTERNAL'. Page 372's Format 1 of the SAME entry does carry a Figure-notes paragraph listing its underlines, so the FD entry is now documented inconsistently across its three formats. The formats are also emitted as loose prose lines rather than inside a fenced block, unlike every other general format in clause 13.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED independently, and the claim actually understates the loss. (1) The PDF underlining is real. I rendered page 373 at 300 dpi and cropped three regions. In the BLOCK clause crop, 'BLOCK' carries a horizontal rule beneath it and 'CONTAINS' immediately to its right does not; 'TO' carries a rule; in the vertical CHARACTERS/RECORDS choice brace, 'CHARACTERS' (upper alternative) has NO rule beneath it while 'RECORDS' directly below it DOES — exactly as claimed. In the REPORT crop, 'REPORT' and 'REPORTS' each carry a rule that stops before the following 'IS'/'ARE', which are unruled. In the FD/EXTERNAL crop, 'FD' is ruled, 'IS' is not, 'EXTERNAL' and 'AS' are. In the CODE-SET crop, 'CODE-SET', 'ALPHANUMERIC' and 'NATIONAL' are ruled while 'IS' and 'FOR' are not. (2) The markdown genuinely carries none of it. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines for the page-373 block (between the page-373 and page-374 anchors) contain zero '<u>' tags, zero code fences, zero 'Figure notes' paragraphs and zero choice-indicator bars. (3) This is NOT a global transcription convention, which is the refutation I looked hardest for and could not sustain. Clause 13 of this same markdown records printed underlining in two established ways: 41 inline '<u>...</u>' tags and 59 '> **Figure notes ...**' paragraphs. Page 372's Format 1 of THIS VERY ENTRY is fenced and followed by a Figure-notes paragraph that enumerates its underlined words verbatim; the immediately following SD entry (13.4.6.2) is unfenced prose yet still writes '<u>SD</u>'. Formats 2 and 3 use neither mechanism, so the information is absent rather than merely re-encoded. (4) I also checked reflow/adjacency: there is no underline record for these formats anywhere on the page, on page 372 after Format 1's own notes, or on page 374. Not a wrapping, hyphenation or page-break artifact. Two parts of the claim's framing are inaccurate but do not touch the substance: the count is twelve underlined words, not eleven, and 'unlike every other general format in clause 13' is overstated — roughly 35 of 78 general-format headings in clause 13 are not followed by a fence within 13 lines, so the missing fence is a cosmetic secondary issue, not the discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description:
Page 373's Format 2 and Format 3 of the file description entry (13.4.5.2) are transcribed as loose prose with every trace of the printed diagram markup stripped, while the same entry's Format 1 on page 372 is fully documented. Two distinct losses, the second more severe than the claim reports.

LOSS 1 — required-word underlining (twelve words, not eleven). The print underlines FD, EXTERNAL, AS, GLOBAL, BLOCK, TO, RECORDS (Format 2 and 3), plus CODE-SET, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL, REPORT, REPORTS (Format 3). It deliberately leaves IS, CONTAINS, CHARACTERS, FOR and ARE unruled. Verified at 300 dpi: 'CHARACTERS' has no rule while 'RECORDS' directly beneath it does; the rules under 'REPORT'/'REPORTS' stop before 'IS'/'ARE'. The markdown records none of this, so the reader cannot tell that CHARACTERS is an optional word, that RECORDS is required, or that 'IS' may be omitted from 'IS EXTERNAL' / 'IS GLOBAL'. This is a real omission and not a house style: clause 13 of the same file records underlining 41 times with inline '<u>' tags and 59 times with 'Figure notes' paragraphs, including page 372's Format 1 of this entry and the unfenced SD entry at 13.4.6.2 which still writes '<u>SD</u>'.

LOSS 2 — NORMATIVE, not merely typographic: Format 3's CODE-SET clause loses its CHOICE INDICATORS. In the print, the inner brace of the CODE-SET second alternative encloses 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1' and 'FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2' between visible vertical bars on both sides of the two phrases (clearly present in the 300 dpi crop). Per 5.2.6.4, braces enclosing choice indicators mean one or more of the enclosed alternatives shall be specified, each at most once, in any order — so a single CODE-SET clause may legally carry the FOR ALPHANUMERIC phrase alone, the FOR NATIONAL phrase alone, or BOTH, in either order. The markdown renders it as a plain either/or brace, '{ FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 / FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 }', which reads as 'specify exactly one'. Page 372's Figure notes call out this exact construct in Format 1 and state that both phrases are permitted, so the transcription now contradicts itself on the legality of 'CODE-SET FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS a1 FOR NATIONAL IS a2' in a report FD. Severity should be raised from structural to semantic on the strength of this second loss.

The missing code fence is real but incidental — many clause-13 general formats are unfenced prose and still carry their markup; the fix is to fence Formats 2 and 3 as page 372 does and attach a Figure-notes paragraph listing the twelve underlined words and the CODE-SET choice indicators.
